title: Cache telemetry perf/overhead bench results (runtime instrumentation)
content:
Doc intent
- Summarize runtime perf impact (latency/throughput/cpu) of new prefix/KV cache telemetry.
- Compare baseline vs instrumentation enabled at different sampling rates.
- Identify safe defaults + canary thresholds.

Scope / what’s included
- New runtime metrics: kv_cache hit/miss counters, prefix cache reuse histograms, eviction/pressure signals, wasted_prefill.
- Sampling + local rate limiting (per PR-18425).
- No tracing/span annotation overhead included here (that has separate canary coverage).

Environment
- Runner: perf-lab (isolated), same host kernel + driver across runs
- Build: redwood-runtime @ 2025-03-11 nightly (includes PR-18421/22/23/24/25)
- GPU configs:
  1) H100 SXM 80GB (CUDA 12.3, driver 550.xx)
  2) A100 SXM 80GB (CUDA 12.2, driver 535.xx)
- Model: llama-3-70b-instruct (quant: fp16), single replica
- Runtime knobs (common): continuous batching ON, prefix cache ON, kv cache ON

Workloads
W1: Chat-like short prompts
- prompt_tokens: ~220 (p50), max 512
- max_new_tokens: 128
- concurrency: 64
- request pattern: repeated system+tool preamble across turns (prefix cache friendly)

W2: Mixed prompt lengths (prod-ish)
- prompt_tokens buckets: 0–256 / 256–1k / 1k–4k distributed 60/30/10
- max_new_tokens: 256
- concurrency: 96
- request pattern: ~30% near-duplicate prefixes, rest unique

W3: Long-context retrieval (stress)
- prompt_tokens: ~3.2k (p50), max 8k
- max_new_tokens: 64
- concurrency: 32
- request pattern: low prefix reuse, higher KV churn

Instrumentation configurations tested
C0: Baseline
- cache telemetry flags OFF

C1: Telemetry enabled, sampling = 1.0
- counters/histos emitted for every request
- local metric aggregation enabled (per-thread batching)

C2: Telemetry enabled, sampling = 0.1 (recommended prod default)
- 10% request sampling for high-volume events (hit/miss + reuse histos)
- eviction/pressure gauges still emitted (low frequency)

C3: Telemetry enabled, sampling = 0.02 (ultra conservative)
- used to bound worst-case cardinality/cost in hosted peaks

Notes on measurement
- Each cell: median of 5 runs (warm caches, 3 min steady state, discard first 30s)
- Latency reported is end-to-end request latency (gateway bypassed; direct runtime RPC)
- Throughput is decode tokens/sec (aggregate) unless otherwise noted
- CPU overhead is runtime process CPU% (host) averaged over steady window

Results table (H100 80GB)
Metric units: latency ms, throughput tok/s, CPU %

W1 (short prompts, high reuse)
Config | p50 | p95 | p99 | Throughput | CPU
C0     | 74  | 132 | 168 |  118,400   |  92%
C1     | 75  | 136 | 173 |  117,100   |  96%
C2     | 74  | 133 | 169 |  118,000   |  93%
C3     | 74  | 132 | 168 |  118,300   |  92%

Delta vs baseline (W1):
- C1: +3.0% p95, -1.1% throughput, +4 CPU pts
- C2: +0.8% p95, -0.3% throughput, +1 CPU pt
- C3: ~0% within noise

W2 (mixed prompt lengths)
Config | p50 | p95 | p99 | Throughput | CPU
C0     | 119 | 224 | 286 |   96,700   |  94%
C1     | 121 | 231 | 297 |   95,100   |  98%
C2     | 120 | 226 | 289 |   96,300   |  95%
C3     | 119 | 225 | 288 |   96,500   |  94%

Delta vs baseline (W2):
- C1: +3.1% p95, -1.7% throughput, +4 CPU pts
- C2: +0.9% p95, -0.4% throughput, +1 CPU pt

W3 (long context, low reuse)
Config | p50 | p95 | p99 | Throughput | CPU
C0     | 341 | 612 | 781 |   41,900   |  88%
C1     | 346 | 628 | 807 |   41,100   |  92%
C2     | 343 | 617 | 790 |   41,700   |  89%
C3     | 342 | 614 | 785 |   41,800   |  88%

Delta vs baseline (W3):
- C1: +2.6% p95, -1.9% throughput, +4 CPU pts
- C2: +0.8% p95, -0.5% throughput, +1 CPU pt

Results table (A100 80GB)
W2 only (mixed prompt lengths) — A100 shows slightly higher sensitivity to CPU contention
Config | p50 | p95 | p99 | Throughput | CPU
C0     | 156 | 292 | 371 |   61,800   |  91%
C1     | 160 | 304 | 387 |   60,300   |  96%
C2     | 157 | 295 | 375 |   61,400   |  92%
C3     | 156 | 293 | 372 |   61,600   |  91%

Delta vs baseline (A100 W2):
- C1: +4.1% p95, -2.4% throughput, +5 CPU pts
- C2: +1.0% p95, -0.6% throughput, +1 CPU pt

Interpretation / notes
- The dominant overhead at sampling=1.0 is histogram/counter emission cost under high QPS + lock contention in the exporter path.
- Sampling=0.1 keeps p95 regression under ~1% across workloads and GPUs; throughput change stays <1%.
- CPU increase at 0.1 sampling is consistently ~+1 pt; at 1.0 it’s +4–5 pts.
- Long-context workload (W3) is mostly GPU-bound; overhead manifests mainly as tail latency jitter (p99) when the exporter runs during prefill completion.
- No evidence of increased GPU memory usage attributable to telemetry (expected; only counters/histos/gauges).

Sampling recommendations (proposed defaults)
- Prod default: sampling=0.1 for high-volume per-request events (hit/miss, reuse histos, wasted_prefill).
- Keep eviction/pressure gauges at full fidelity (already low frequency).
- Allow per-route override only in canary/staging (avoid customers enabling 1.0 inadvertently).

Perf-canary gating suggestion (ties to perf-canary/pr-287)
- Canary failure threshold (initial):
  - p95 latency regression > 2.0% for 15 min window OR
  - throughput regression > 2.0% for 15 min window
- With sampling=0.1, we’re comfortably inside the 2% gate across tested workloads.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Exporter batching interval: we used current default (50ms). Would like to test 50ms vs 100ms for further tail smoothing.
- Need to rerun once PR-18432 (trace span annotations) is in; ensure trace annotations don’t reintroduce p99 jitter under W3.
- Validate overhead when gateway tags are fully enabled (route/model/version allowlist) — minor string processing expected; should stay near noise with cached label objects.

Action items
- Marcus: post summary in #eng-runtime and attach this doc link; recommend sampling=0.1 default (ETA 2025-03-13)
- Samir/Omar: confirm runtime flag defaults in PR-18429 / release notes (sampling=0.1, telemetry OFF in dev by default?)
- Allison: ensure dashboards/alerts assume sampling and use rate() appropriately (don’t treat sampled counters as absolute counts without scaling notes)

Appendix: raw run IDs (perf-lab)
- H100 W1: runset h100-w1-20250311-01 .. -05
- H100 W2: runset h100-w2-20250311-01 .. -05
- H100 W3: runset h100-w3-20250311-01 .. -05
- A100 W2: runset a100-w2-20250311-01 .. -05
